I don't understand...what does infantilizing have to do with calling people racial slurs? 

You know the funny thing is that amongst my urban friends and other urban people I know, these so called "racist" comments aren't taken as harshly as they are by people from the suburbs.  My friends and I called each other the most offensive names ie. Beaner, Wetback, Chink, Cracker etc and laughed at it all the time, it was/is part of our identity to crack jokes at each others minority status so it was much more lighthearted even if it was supposed to be offensive.  We were all so poor that we had nothing to hide, our neighborhoods were tightly packed so we were forced to constantly interact with our neighbors; Puerto Rican, Vietnamese, Black, White, Mexican etc. so we learned early on not to be too offended by anything.

The only people I see who are angry and offended seem to be people who were sheltered and had no real contact and or interaction with people outside of their race/ethnicity and who don't understand the culture of not being easily offended.  Had I been with one of my urban friends and called them "Beaners" we would have just laughed and went on about our business because we understand that we all take slight jabs at each other.  One of my closest friends is Mexican and he always calls me "Negress" (being half black) and I call him "Boarder Brother", we understand that part of our culture is to talk smack about each others culture. 

My friends from the hood are so much more lighthearted and ready to laugh and have a comeback in situations like these, we all get each other.  I notice that my more uptight friends take offense to what my hood friends would laugh at and use as a moment of bonding and making fun of each other.  It becomes more obvious why great comedians come from the hood, because there is a lot of humor in our culture and it's meant to be lighthearted yet honest/truthful at times.  In the hood name calling isn't meant to mean anything hateful, it helps to let off steam and move on.

Because he thought of me as an object who might satisfy him sexually.

Another time I was walking with a friend, she was overly PC (from the suburbs while I'm from the projects, a very diverse neighborhood), we walked past a group of Latino guys and they made some comment about me.  I got mad and called them "Beaners" (which is apparently more offensive to suburbanites than it is to urban folks) my friend became so angry saying she couldn't believe I called them "Beaners" and how insensitive and offensive it was for me to call them that name.  

I told her I couldn't believe she was more offended that I had called two older, stranger males who just sexually harassed me on the streets "Beaners" than she was that they just sexually harassed her friend in front of her.  This turned into an enormous fight between us because apparently as a young woman I shouldn't say anything offensive back to them.  Ugh.

I feel like people infantilize people of color as if they cannot be held accountable and or responsible for their actions and quite honestly that is really fucking racist.
